ruled_out.background_passes: dispatch / workflows / scheduler / business each a few ms

root_cause: fleet/service.py:162 puts every mission with a version into the refresh set when the service starts (the M2 rule to reconcile persisted input after a restart); the first pass of the background loop refreshes all of them synchronously, so the API on the same event loop does not answer until it finishes

each refresh rechecks every evidence image through the verifier, which recomputes image quality pixel by pixel in Python (about 0.1 s per image), and reads the mission's journals several times from the events table, which has no index usable by mission_id and is scanned in full
the desk accumulates about 170 missions a day, so the blocked start grows linearly; after 72 h it exceeded the frozen 60 s limit

related_findings.steady_state_service_cpu: 3.5% to 30.6% over the soak; the refresh path (evidence recheck, full scans of events) grows with the ledger; not a criterion
related_findings.desk_dock_memory: about 4 MiB/h, reset by the daily residents restart, peaked above 95% of 128 MiB (reported, not a criterion)
related_findings.desk_fleet: memory about 7 MiB/h and CPU 1.7% to about 20%; its onboard uplink rescans every accepted mission each cycle (onboard M2 code, unchanged by P5)

next: fix without a schema change (bounded, prioritised startup reconciliation off the API path; reuse a persisted verification for unchanged evidence bytes), test, new candidate, and a new full 72 h soak per D073; an index on events(mission_id, mission_version) is a schema change and needs approval first
